To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the silica sol hybridized with PCL solution significantly improved the physicochemical properties and in vitro drug release of nanofibrous PCL scaffolds, and thus, the hybrid nanofibers can be applied for GBR.

the hybridization of the PCL polymer with the silica sol remarkably improved the physicochemical and mechanical properties of the nanofibrous scaffold, and enhanced the drug-loading efficiency and drug release rate of the drug-loaded scaffold.

the silica sol content of the electrospinning solution significantly affected the physicochemical, mechanical and biological properties of the hybrid scaffolds, while maintaining their intrinsic properties of the PCL polymer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new hybrid nanofibers with improved mechanical properties and enhanced drug-loading efficiency for GBR applications.
the development of a novel hybrid nanofibrousscaffold for GBR.
the synthesis and characterization of PCL/silica hybrid nanofiber scaffolds loaded with TCH drug, which are expected to be useful for bone tissue regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hybridization of the PCL solution and the silica sol can be a promising approach for the fabrication of drug-loaded PCL/silica hybrid nanofiberous scaffolds with improved properties and functions.
the hybridization of the silica sol with the PCL solution can be an effective approach to improve the physicochemical properties and drug release behavior of the electrospun nanofibrous scaffold.

the hybridization of the PCL solution by the silica sol can be an effective approach to produce drug-loaded PCL/silica hybrid nanofiberous scaffolds with improved drug loading and sustained release, and enhanced mechanical and biocompatibility properties for the GBR application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hybridization of silica sol in PCL nanofibrous scaffold can be an effective approach to enhance mechanical properties, hydrophilicity, and drug loading and release properties, which are important factors to be considered in GBR applications.
the hybrid scaffolds produced by the present study have great potential to be applied to the GBR technique as drug delivery scaffolds.
the hybrid nanofibers have great potential for use as GBR scaffolds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

hybrid nanofibers with high loading efficiency, high hydrophilicity, and high mechanical properties can be fabricated by hybridizing PCL with a small amount of silica sol and can be potentially applied to the GBR.

the hybridization of silica sol with PCL nanofibers could be a useful approach for the production of drug-loaded nanofibrous GBR scaffolds with enhanced drug loading efficiency, hydrophilicity, mechanical properties, and drug release behavior.
hybridization of silica sol in PCL solution using electrospinning could be a promising approach for the development of drug-loaded hybrid scaffolds for GBR applications.
